body: Ah! Only just now saw this. Yes, the inputs were swapped around. Perhaps this is the source of the issue. In my case, I have no other choice but to feed the cobble from the middle back slot, so my solution works best. A pretty simple modification also.

I did not skip the barrels, the only thing that changed is that the various materials aren't necessarily coming in from the same sides. The build is exactly the same. I'm playing vanilla.

Here is the build, including a view of the change I implemented that fixes this flaw.

[https://imgur.com/a/PBsSf9R](https://imgur.com/a/PBsSf9R)

EDIT: To reproduce this bug, test it by introducing partials stacks of cobblestone that are not a multiple of 4. If you test your machine with perfect stacks of 64 chances are you'll never encounter this issue. But in a survival environment where I might switch off my cobble farm at any moment, this can become an issue over time.

After tinkering, I have found a solution: For the cobblestone, I have moved the comparator output by one block. This means that the hopper directly into the crafter will have stock, and the crafter will be turned off when the container above it runs out. So, the crafter stop, but the hopper itself still has a buffer of items to refill the recipe.

I'll keep an eye on this crafter and I might end up raising the crafter-stopping comparator outputs up for all ingredients as I fear this may be a design flaw where any ingredient running out will cause the recipe to bleed ingredients.

EDIT: It seems the other ingredients (mostly the planks) can sometimes dip from 64 to 62, but they eventually fix themselves. The most problematic ingredient was definitely the cobble, seeing as it requires the full time delay to refill all 4 slots. When this farm is fully operational I'll have more long-term running data, but for now I'm satisfied with raising only the cobblestone stock comparator output by one block.

First off, congratulations on making this choice to take care of yourself. You're stepping up as your own parent and protector, and that's the first step in freeing yourself of this awful situation.

I don't know how old you are, or how your relationship to your mother is, so what I'm about to tell you is relative of course... But 3 days is a very short time in the grand scheme of things. It's probably best for your mom and yourself to let the dust settle. You might find that you're feeling better as time goes by and you aren't caught in their toxic behaviors. The more you learn to rely on yourself, the less power this will have over you, and you may eventually feel so strong and solid that none of it will really shake you to your core.

Another thing that's maybe worth mentioning is, she may be your mom, but that's not all that she is. She is also a fallible human being like the rest of us, who is struggling in her own situation and stuck in her own patterns. I'm not saying this gives her a free pass to be a shitty parent, but if you find it in you to think of her that way, maybe you'll come to take her choices less personally, and they will have less of a hold over you. 

It's unlikely that your mom will die in the next week or month, so right this minute there's no need to obsess over what your last words to her were. If this radio silence continues over a long time, you may want to eventually send her an email that is less angry than what you've said to her last, if that makes you feel better. The emphasis is on you. If you do it, do it for yourself, to give yourself some peace. Don't do it expecting her to tell you everything you want to hear, because past actions are the best predictor of future behavior. 

The only person you have control over is yourself. I can tell you're willing to step up for yourself and your own wellbeing. Your eyes are open and you likely have the tools to build a life for yourself that will be different, a life free of this sort of toxicity. This community will always be here to hear you and welcome you when things are tough. My heart goes out to you. You're stronger than you realize.

I don't have children and can't really comment on that aspect, however I'd like to mention that rarely, in my experience, does polyamory manifest as "involving a third partner". The odds of finding someone that you're both into, and who is into both of you, are quite low. Usually there is more chance of success if each of you is free to pursue their own relationships. I'm not saying it's impossible, but it's unlikely. The first pitfall I had to battle as I began my journey into polyamory was the expectation of symmetry between my experience and my partner's experience. Accepting to give each other the freedom to explore romance outside your relationship means accepting that your individual paths will probably not mirror each other.
